source.section: PA-40 lines 1a to 12 (form pages 1-2); PDF page 1 and form line 12 rate 3.07 percent; PDF page 9 no standard deduction or exemptions; PDF page 20 Lines 9 and 10; PDF page 21 Lines 11 and 12; PDF pages 36-39 PA Schedule SP Sections III and IV and Eligibility Income Tables 1 and 2 (PDF page 39); PA-40 lines 19a to 21; projection: Tax Forgiveness is not_modelled, not applied; PDF page 8 'INCOME NOT TAXABLE FOR PA PIT PURPOSES' first bullet; the PA-40 has no Social Security line

worked: The approximation's couple: 90,000.00 of exempt pension and Social Security income, 12,000.00 of interest and dividends. Federal AGI = private pension person 0 70,000.00 + taxable Social Security 17,000.00 + interest 5,000.00 + dividends 7,000.00 = 99,000.00. Taxable Social Security is the federal worksheet's result on the gross benefit and other income. Federal taxable income = 99,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 + age 65 addition 3,200.00 = 64,300.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Pennsylvania, as the projection works it: start federal AGI 99,000.00; less 70,000.00 private pension person 0 (pa_employer_plans); less 17,000.00 taxable Social Security (social_security exempt; gross 20,000.00; no PA line); income after reliefs = 12,000.00. No standard deduction or exemption (PDF page 9), no Line 10 deduction: state taxable income 12,000.00. Tax = 12,000.00 x 0.0307 = 368.40. No credit in the projection; state income tax 368.40. Form: Line 1a/1c 0.00; Line 2 5,000.00; Line 3 7,000.00; Line 5 0.00; Line 9 12,000.00; Line 10 0.00; Line 11 12,000.00; Line 12 368.40 (the form, in whole dollars, PDF page 4, shows 368). Schedule SP: Eligibility Income 12,000.00 is at or under 13,000.00, Table 2 gives 100 percent, Line 21 is 368.40 and the household owes 0.00. The projection does not apply it and shows 368.40. Expected follows the projection.
accepted_approximations: Pennsylvania has no federal starting point: it adds the positive amounts of eight classes (compensation, interest, dividends, business, gains, rents, estates and trusts, gambling). The mapping runs from federal AGI to those classes: start from federal AGI, then take out what the reliefs below exempt. Wages, interest, dividends, gains, business income and rents are taken as federal AGI holds them, in one sum. The differences that remain are listed one by one in the next four entries.

Tax Forgiveness is not applied. For a low-income or retired household the projection shows PA tax that the household does not owe. Line 9 income for a retiree is mostly interest, dividends and gains, because Social Security, eligible pensions and IRA withdrawals are not PA-taxed, and those three are also left out of Eligibility Income. So the credit depends on that small taxable income and not on total cash income. Eligibility Income also counts things a projection does not see: Treasury and Pennsylvania bond interest, gifts, inheritances, insurance proceeds, survivor annuities and an excluded home-sale gain, which can remove the credit.
